hypothesis: A configuration-driven routing and orchestration layer, deployed via CI/CD with feature flags and canary releases, will (a) reduce p95 end-to-end localization latency and (b) improve throughput per dollar at peak load, without materially increasing error rates or incident frequency, compared to a baseline pipeline with hard-coded routing and ad hoc deployments.

baseline.description: Existing or minimally viable localization pipeline with static routing logic embedded in application code and manual or ad hoc deployments.

architecture.routing: Hard-coded if/else logic for risk, language, and content type inside a monolithic service or script.
architecture.orchestration: Synchronous calls (e.g., REST chain) without a workflow engine or queue; no explicit state machine.
architecture.deployment: Manual or semi-manual deployments (e.g., direct pushes to main or manual container image updates) without dedicated localization-specific CI/CD stages.
architecture.feature_flags: None or coarse-grained toggles at application restart; no per-locale or per-segment flags.
architecture.canary_releases: None; new routing logic and model versions go live to 100% of traffic immediately.
architecture.resilience: Best-effort retries with default library settings; no circuit breakers, backoff policies, or bulkheading.
architecture.observability: Basic request logging and coarse latency metrics; no per-stage breakdown or per-route telemetry.

configuration.routing_rules: Embedded in code; changes require a code change and full redeploy.
configuration.risk_model: Simplistic classification (e.g., boolean high_risk flag) or content type only; no combined multi-attribute routing.
configuration.supported_languages: Fixed list in code; no dynamic additions via configuration.

treatment.description: Configuration-driven routing and orchestration layer, integrated with a workflow engine/queue, deployed via CI/CD with feature flags, canary releases, and explicit resilience patterns.

architecture.routing: Dedicated routing service (e.g., Python FastAPI or similar) that evaluates a configuration-driven rule engine using YAML/JSON rules for risk, language, content type, and channel.
architecture.orchestration: Workflow engine or orchestrator (e.g., Temporal, Airflow, Argo Workflows, or Step Functions) plus a message queue (e.g., SQS, Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ) to manage asynchronous stages: ingest → classify → route → localize → QA → deliver.
architecture.deployment: CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions) with build, test, staging, and production steps; promotion gated on load/performance tests and smoke tests for routing rules.
architecture.feature_flags: Configurable flags (e.g., using a feature flag service or config file) that can enable/disable specific routes, models, or workflows per language, risk level, content type, and traffic percentage.
architecture.canary_releases: Per-route canary policies; a small configurable percentage of matching traffic is routed to new workflows or models first, with automated rollback on metric regressions.
architecture.resilience: Explicit resilience patterns (e.g., exponential backoff, circuit breakers, timeouts, dead-letter queues) applied at each external dependency (MT/LLM providers, QA services).
architecture.observability: Structured per-stage logging and tracing (correlation IDs), metrics for each workflow state, and per-route dashboards for latency, errors, and cost.

configuration.routing_rules: Externalized YAML/JSON-based rules defining decision trees on risk, language, content_type, and channel, including fallback routes and human-in-the-loop escalations.
configuration.risk_model: Configurable mapping from inputs (e.g., regulatory tags, content source) to risk categories that drive different workflows (e.g., `high_risk_pharma_label` vs `low_risk_marketing_banner`).
configuration.supported_languages: Languages and per-language workflows defined in configuration, enabling additions/removals via config-only changes deployed through CI/CD.

workloads.name: WL1-high-risk-product-docs
workloads.description: High-risk, regulated product documentation and labeling content (e.g., pharmaceutical patient leaflets, financial disclosures).

input_profile.arrival_pattern: Bursty: large batches during planned releases plus occasional urgent hotfix segments.

routing_expectation.baseline: Single high-risk workflow regardless of channel or language; full human review hard-coded.
routing_expectation.treatment: Risk-based and channel-aware routing: mandatory human-in-the-loop for most; but specific low-impact sections (e.g., boilerplate legal) may use lighter QA routes as defined in configuration.

workloads.name: WL2-low-risk-marketing-and-ui
workloads.description: Lower-risk marketing content and product UI strings for a web or SaaS product.

input_profile.volume: 20,000–50,000 segments per run; UI strings 5–15 words, marketing snippets 20–80 words.
input_profile.arrival_pattern: Near-continuous trickle with periodic spikes aligned to product releases and campaigns.

routing_expectation.baseline: Uniform MT workflow with optional batch human review; no differentiation by channel or business priority.
routing_expectation.treatment: Config-driven routing that uses lighter workflows (e.g., automated QA only) for low-risk UI strings and optional canary routes for new MT models or prompts on a percentage of traffic.

workloads.name: WL3-peak-load-stress-test
workloads.description: Synthetic peak-volume workload simulating large simultaneous multi-channel updates (e.g., major product launch or regulatory deadline).

input_profile.volume: 100,000–300,000 segments in a compressed time window (e.g., 30–60 minutes).
input_profile.arrival_pattern: Highly concurrent submissions from multiple simulated services; resembles worst-case traffic scenario.

routing_expectation.baseline: Best-effort synchronous processing with increased timeouts and potential request failures or timeouts under load.
routing_expectation.treatment: Queue-based ingestion with backpressure, scalable workers, prioritized processing (e.g., high-risk docs before marketing), and resilience patterns to preserve SLOs.

data.dataset: Use the same underlying content segments for baseline and treatment, drawn from the chapter 5 baseline dataset extended for chapter 10 (stored in the repository under `/data/ch10_routing_orchestration/`).
data.train_test_split: No model training is part of this experiment; however, random seeds and sampling for load generation must be fixed across baseline and treatment (e.g., `SEED=42`).

environment.infrastructure: Same cloud region, VM/container instance types, autoscaling settings, and network configuration for baseline and treatment.
environment.dependencies: Identical versions of MT/LLM APIs, QA services, and supporting libraries; pinned via requirements.txt/poetry.lock and container images.
environment.secrets: Same API keys and quotas across conditions; ensure no rate limiting differences.

routing_inputs.classification: Use the same upstream content classification (risk, channel, content_type) inputs for both baseline and treatment; only routing/orchestration behavior may differ.
routing_inputs.localization_logic: Do not change underlying translation models or QA rules between baseline and treatment during this experiment; isolate the effect of routing, orchestration, and CI/CD deployment practices.

run_conditions.time_window: Run baseline and treatment experiments in close temporal proximity to minimize external fluctuations (e.g., within the same 24-hour period).
run_conditions.parallelism: If executing baseline and treatment concurrently, ensure isolation of resources or clear accounting for resource sharing; preferred approach is sequential runs with cooldown periods.

metrics.name: end_to_end_latency_p50
metrics.description: Median latency from content ingestion to localized artifact ready for consumption.

metrics.name: end_to_end_latency_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile latency from content ingestion to localized artifact, emphasizing tail performance under load.

metrics.name: throughput
metrics.description: Sustained processing rate for each workload during steady-state operation.

metrics.name: cost_per_segment
metrics.description: Estimated total cost per segment, including MT/LLM API usage, QA services, and proportional infrastructure costs.

metrics.name: error_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of segments that fail to complete successfully due to technical errors (HTTP 5xx, workflow failures, timeouts beyond retries) or are routed to dead-letter queues.

metrics.name: rollback_events
metrics.description: Number of times a deployment or canary route had to be rolled back due to metric regression or incident.

metrics.name: incident_rate
metrics.description: Number of distinct incidents recorded (e.g., SEV2+ workflow or routing incidents) during or immediately after the experiment run.

metrics.name: routing_accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of segments that follow the intended route as defined by the experiment's ground-truth routing policy (e.g., high-risk content must pass through human review checkpoints).

metrics.name: queue_depth_p95
metrics.description: 95th percentile depth of key queues (ingest, localization, QA) during peak load, as a proxy for system stress and backpressure management.

primary.description: Treatment improves or maintains tail latency and throughput compared to baseline without increasing error rate.
conditions: For each workload (WL1, WL2, WL3), treatment end_to_end_latency_p95 <= baseline end_to_end_latency_p95 * 1.05 (no more than 5% worse) and at least one workload shows >= 10% improvement.
For each workload, treatment throughput >= baseline throughput * 1.10 (at least 10% higher) OR maintains throughput with significantly reduced queue_depth_p95 (>= 20% reduction).
For each workload, treatment error_rate <= baseline error_rate * 1.10 (no more than 10% increase) and no absolute error_rate > 0.03 (3%).

secondary.description: Treatment reduces cost per segment or improves cost efficiency.
conditions: For at least one workload, treatment cost_per_segment <= baseline cost_per_segment * 0.95 (at least 5% lower) OR demonstrates improved throughput at equal cost (throughput increase >= 10% at +/- 2% cost_per_segment).

secondary.description: Treatment improves operational safety and control.
conditions: routing_accuracy in treatment >= 0.98 for high-risk routes in WL1.
rollback_events_treatment >= 1 across experiments OR capability to perform automated rollback is validated via deliberate canary failure injection.
incident_rate_treatment <= incident_rate_baseline + 1 (allowing minor issues during initial adoption) and no SEV1 incidents attributable to routing/orchestration defects.

success_criteria.acceptance: Experiment is considered successful if all primary criteria are met and at least one secondary criterion is met without violating operational safety (no SEV1 incidents or compliance-critical routing errors).

failure_modes.name: misrouting_high_risk_content
failure_modes.description: High-risk segments (e.g., regulatory docs) are incorrectly routed to low-control workflows (e.g., no human review) due to rule misconfiguration or classification errors.
failure_modes.detection: Discrepancy between expected route (from ground-truth mapping) and actual route in logs; compliance or reviewer audits find missing checkpoints.
failure_modes.mitigation: Add validation tests for routing rules in CI; enforce explicit whitelists for high-risk patterns that always require human-in-the-loop; implement runtime guardrails that prevent fully automated release for regulated channels.

failure_modes.name: queue_overload_and_starvation
failure_modes.description: Under peak load, queues grow without bound or low-priority content starves high-risk workflows.
failure_modes.detection: queue_depth_p95 significantly higher in treatment, SLA breaches for WL1 while WL2/3 continue consuming capacity.
failure_modes.mitigation: Introduce queue priority mechanisms; rate-limit low-priority workloads; add autoscaling triggers on queue depth with upper bounds.

failure_modes.name: orchestrator_bottleneck
failure_modes.description: Central workflow engine or routing service becomes a performance bottleneck, increasing latency and error rate.
failure_modes.detection: High CPU/memory utilization on orchestrator nodes, increased orchestrator response times, timeouts on orchestration calls.
failure_modes.mitigation: Scale out orchestrator instances; optimize workflow definitions; cache static decisions; use sharding or partitioning of workflows when possible.

failure_modes.name: feature_flag_or_canary_misconfiguration
failure_modes.description: Incorrect feature flag settings route too much traffic to experimental workflows or prevent rollback.
failure_modes.detection: Sudden spikes in error_rate or latency correlated with flag changes; discrepancies between intended and actual traffic allocations.
failure_modes.mitigation: Introduce flag change approval and change logs; simulate flag configurations in staging; add guardrails that cap canary traffic (e.g., max 20%) without explicit override.

failure_modes.name: CI_CD_pipeline_regression
failure_modes.description: New routing configurations or workflow definitions pass CI but break at runtime due to insufficient tests or environment drift.
failure_modes.detection: Increased incident_rate immediately after deployments; failures in smoke/load tests; rollback_events triggered frequently.
failure_modes.mitigation: Strengthen integration and end-to-end tests that cover routing trees; enforce blue/green or canary deployments for orchestrator and routing services; snapshot production configs before changes for quick rollback.

failure_modes.name: cost_explosion_under_treatment
failure_modes.description: More sophisticated routing and resilience patterns inadvertently increase cost_per_segment (e.g., due to retries or extra QA passes).
failure_modes.detection: treatment cost_per_segment > baseline cost_per_segment * 1.20; large share of cost attributed to retries or redundant stages.
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement retry budgets and cost-aware routing heuristics; tune backoff and timeout settings; audit workflow paths for redundant steps.

runtime.language: Python 3.10+ for workflow logic and routing services.
runtime.config_format: YAML/JSON for routing rules and workflow definitions.
runtime.containerization: Docker or compatible container runtime for orchestrator, routing service, and worker services.

dependencies.python_packages: Listed in `ch10_routing_orchestration/requirements.txt` or `pyproject.toml` (e.g., FastAPI/Flask, pydantic, requests/httpx, orchestration SDK, queue client, logging and metrics libraries).
dependencies.orchestration_tool: One of: Temporal, Airflow, Argo Workflows, or AWS Step Functions. Experiment scripts should abstract specifics; exact choice must be recorded in evidence.
dependencies.queue_service: One of: AWS SQS, GCP Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ, or Kafka as defined in configuration.
dependencies.monitoring: Metrics backend (e.g., Prometheus, CloudWatch, Stackdriver) and centralized logging (e.g., ELK/Opensearch, Cloud Logging).

environment_types: staging: representative but smaller-scale environment for dry runs.
production-like: environment with capacity and configuration comparable to production for final experiment runs.
infrastructure.compute: Kubernetes cluster or equivalent container orchestration environment OR VMs with container runtime; sufficient nodes to simulate peak load for WL3.
infrastructure.network: Stable network connectivity to MT/LLM and QA providers; latency variations should be monitored.

secrets_and_access.secrets_manager: Use a centralized secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) referenced in configuration; do not hardcode credentials.
secrets_and_access.permissions: Experiment runner needs deployment permissions for staging and production-like environments, and read access to logs/metrics.

run_instructions: Clone the repository and check out the chapter 10 branch or tag (e.g., `git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance.git && cd ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance && git checkout ch10-routing-orchestration`).

Build and start the baseline environment:
  - Navigate to `/ch05_baseline_pipeline/`.
  - Build Docker images: `docker compose build` (or equivalent script).
  - Start services: `docker compose up -d`.
  - Verify health endpoints for baseline services.

Prepare the experiment datasets:
  - Ensure `/data/ch10_routing_orchestration/` contains workload definitions and input segments for WL1, WL2, WL3.
  - Confirm that each segment has stable IDs and metadata (language, channel, content_type, risk_level).

Configure experiment settings:
  - In `/ch10_routing_orchestration/config/experiment.yaml`, set:
    - `workloads`: WL1, WL2, WL3 definitions and volumes.
    - `seed`: fixed random seed (e.g., 42).
    - `orchestrator_type` and `queue_type` consistent across baseline and treatment.
    - `routing_ground_truth`: reference file mapping segments to expected routes for routing_accuracy computation.

Run baseline experiment:
  - Use provided script, e.g., `python run_experiment.py --mode baseline --config config/experiment.yaml`.
  - The runner should:
    - Feed workloads into the baseline pipeline at configured arrival patterns.
    - Collect per-segment timing, route (if any), errors, and cost data.
    - Export results to `/results/ch10/baseline/{timestamp}/` as JSON/Parquet/CSV plus summary metrics.

Tear down or isolate baseline environment:
  - `docker compose down` for baseline, or ensure resource separation if keeping it running.
  - Archive baseline logs and metrics; record environment versions (container SHAs, git commit hash).

Build and start treatment environment:
  - Navigate to `/ch10_routing_orchestration/`.
  - Build images: `docker compose build`.
  - Apply database or orchestrator migrations if needed (e.g., `alembic upgrade head`, `orchestratorctl apply workflows`).
  - Start services: `docker compose up -d`.

Deploy routing configuration via CI/CD simulation:
  - Commit or update routing rules in `config/routing_rules.yaml` and push to the experiment branch.
  - Trigger CI/CD pipeline locally or via remote (e.g., `gh workflow run ch10-routing.yml`).
  - Ensure pipeline stages: lint, unit tests (including routing rule tests), integration tests, deploy to staging, smoke test, deploy to production-like.

Enable feature flags and canary settings for treatment:
  - Define flags in `config/feature_flags.yaml` (or external feature flag service) for:
    - New routing paths (e.g., `use_workflow_high_risk_v2`).
    - Canary percentages per workload.
  - Start with low traffic percentages (e.g., 10%) for canary routes.

Run treatment experiment:
  - Execute `python run_experiment.py --mode treatment --config config/experiment.yaml`.
  - Confirm that:
    - Same input segments and arrival patterns are used as in baseline (validated via segment IDs and seed).
    - CI/CD pipeline logs deployment history for this run.
  - Collect per-segment and per-stage telemetry; store under `/results/ch10/treatment/{timestamp}/`.

Monitor metrics during runs:
  - Use dashboards or CLI tools to watch latency (p50/p95), throughput, error_rate, queue_depth, and incident/alert streams.
  - If automated rollback triggers (e.g., due to p95 or error SLO violation), record the event ID and reason.

Post-run analysis:
  - Run analysis notebook or script, e.g., `python analyze_results.py --baseline /results/ch10/baseline/{timestamp}/ --treatment /results/ch10/treatment/{timestamp}/`.
  - Compute metrics specified in `metrics` for each workload and globally.
  - Compute routing_accuracy by comparing actual routes vs. `routing_ground_truth`.
Document outcomes and environment details in a structured evidence artifact as per `evidence_schema` and store under `/results/ch10/evidence/{timestamp}.json`.

If failure modes are detected (e.g., misrouting, severe regressions), halt further canary expansion, roll back routing/orchestration changes, and open incident and change records referencing the experiment ID.

experiment_id.description: Identifier of the experiment; should match the top-level experiment_id.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for when the experiment was completed.

git_commit.description: Git commit hash(es) for baseline and treatment code used in the experiment.

environment.description: Description of infrastructure and orchestration tools used.

workloads.description: List of workloads included in the experiment and their parameters.

conditions.description: High-level conditions for baseline and treatment runs.

baseline_metrics.description: Aggregated metrics for baseline runs per workload and overall.

treatment_metrics.description: Aggregated metrics for treatment runs per workload and overall.

comparative_analysis.description: Computed differences between baseline and treatment and whether success criteria were met.

overall_success.description: True if overall experiment met defined success_criteria.

routing_validation.description: Results of validating actual routing decisions against expected ground truth.

deployments_and_rollbacks.description: List of deployments, canary promotions, and rollback events during the experiment.

incidents.description: Operational incidents recorded during or immediately after experiment runs.

interpretation.description: Human-authored interpretation of experiment results and implications for production adoption.
